title: Richard the Lionheart and the Third Crusade
welcome_lead: Travel to the eastern Mediterranean in the 1190s, where English king Richard I and Ayyubid sultan Saladin clashed over the Holy Land.
meta_desc: History Prescribed Subjects Adventure 2: Richard the Lionheart, the Third Crusade and the struggle for Jerusalem.

walkthroughs.body_html: Saladin's decisive defeat of the Crusader states at the Battle of Hattin in 1187 and his subsequent capture of Jerusalem provoked a horrified response in Latin Christendom. Pope Gregory VIII's bull Audita tremendi called for a new crusade. Three monarchs — Frederick Barbarossa of the Holy Roman Empire, Philip II of France and Richard I of England — pledged to take the Cross.

After Frederick drowned and Philip returned home, Richard became the dominant Latin commander. He captured Cyprus in 1191, joined the long siege of Acre, won the Battle of Arsuf and twice came within striking distance of Jerusalem before logistical realities forced him back. His relationship with Saladin combined military rivalry with mutual respect.

The Treaty of Jaffa (1192) left Jerusalem in Muslim hands but secured a strip of coast for the Crusader states and pilgrim access to the holy sites. Richard's return journey ended in captivity by Duke Leopold of Austria and an enormous ransom paid by his subjects. He died in 1199 besieging a French castle.
